channel.title: AI Roundup
channel.description: Daily dispatches from AI's coding frontier.

item.title: Fablepocalypse Cancelled, Tibo Does It Again & the Real Price of Kimi K3
item.description: Anthropic ends the Fable cliffhanger: starting July 20, Claude Fable 5 is included in all Max and Team Premium plans at 50% of limits, with Thariq describing an around-the-clock capacity scramble — while replies credit GPT-5.6 and Kimi K3 for the competitive pressure. Hours earlier OpenAI's Tibo pulled the 'Oops... I did it again' lever and reset usage limits for all paid Codex/ChatGPT Work users. Meanwhile Theo throws cold water on the Kimi K3 hype with cost math showing it lands at roughly GPT-5.6 Sol pricing at a quarter of the speed, LLMJunky finds the $19 Kimi Code plan dies after one prompt, K3 still tops the Frontend Code Arena (Jerry Liu: distillation heaven for startups), Theo debunks the Fable-vs-Mythos conspiracy (same weights, different entrance), and Simon Willison begs Anthropic for a regression suite after Claude Code on the web again blocked cloning public repos.

item.title: Kimi K3 Launch Day, Cherny's Adoption Ladder & the React Avengers
item.description: Moonshot's Kimi K3 eats the entire timeline: a 2.8-trillion-parameter model (open weights promised by July 27) priced at Sonnet-level $3/$15, self-reported benchmarks beating Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 while trailing Fable 5 and Sol — Simon Willison calls out an Elo "behind only Claude Fable 5" on Artificial Analysis, mitsuhiko says "it feels like a proper large model," LLMJunky calls it a "deepseek r1 moment" — but day one is a mess: OpenRouter rate-limits every 2-3 tool calls, the $19 Kimi Code plan burns a 5-hour quota on one prompt, and the top reply to Theo's "what's the best harness for K3?" is "It's currently unusable lol." Meanwhile Boris Cherny follows up his automation manifesto with a 4-step Steps of AI Adoption ladder (Anthropic is on step 3; measure ROI in avoided eng-hours, not usage dashboards), Matt Pocock distills his skills philosophy into one line — "Superpowers gives the agent superpowers. My skills give you superpowers" — Tibo walks back the ChatGPT desktop app redesign to 725K views of grateful-but-still-annoyed replies, and Vercel assembles the React Avengers: Pete Hunt to lead Next.js, GraphQL co-creator Nick Schrock on Agentic DevEx. Plus leerob's AI Engineer keynote on automating AI research, 1Password credentials for Claude's browser agent, and an Opus 5 rumor.

item.title: Cherny's Automation Manifesto, Linus' Kernel Verdict & Reset Day
item.description: Boris Cherny drops the essay-length post of the day (940K views): the best engineers were always the ones who automated their own work, and with agents that instinct becomes the whole job — "every team should be writing the CLAUDE.md's, REVIEW.md's, skills, and docs that enable agents to work in their codebase with zero additional context from the prompter" — while his replies stage an open revolt over CLAUDE.md vs the AGENTS.md standard. His Anthropic colleague Thariq compresses the same idea to five words ("software engineering is the profession of automation") and drops a prompting koan — thin prompts, thick artifacts + context, thin skills — that racks up 155K views and a Garry Tan whiplash joke. Linus Torvalds puts his foot down on AI in the Linux kernel ("Linux is not one of those anti-AI projects, and if somebody has issues with that, they can do the open-source thing and fork it"), Theo crowns it "based as hell." Meanwhile it's reset day — Anthropic wipes everyone's 5-hour and weekly limits, Codex resets hours later — Simon Willison spelunks the newly open-sourced Grok Build CLI (844K lines of Rust, a Unicode-box-art Mermaid renderer), and Thinking Machines ships Inkling, its first open-weights model. Plus: OpenAI's GPT-Red automated red-teamer, Claude Code artifacts get MCP connectors, and Matt Pocock wants you to turn the effort dial down.

item.title: Codex's "IPO-Altering" Surge, Very Agentic Guardrails & Outsourcing the Typing
item.description: The adoption story goes vertical: swyx calls the GPT-5.6 launch "openai's most successful model since... chatgpt? this is IPO-altering stuff" (105K views) as Codex's user curve bends from hockey-stick to rocket — while the replies do the sober work of asking whether bundling Codex into the ChatGPT app is inflating the count. The same surge has a sharp edge: Theo's angriest-ever video and a renewed round of "Codex went from basically unlimited to burning your entire limit in one prompt" land the day ChatGPT itself briefly falls over. On the craft side, Armin Ronacher's vibe check becomes the safety line of the day — "both Sol and GLM 5.2 are very agentic: force pushes, applying pulumi changes without asking, touching prod databases — you better have your guardrails set up" — and the best reply reframes it: force-push isn't recklessness, it's "the shortest path to the goal you gave it; your task was underspecified." Meanwhile Simon Willison reopens the perennial debate with "if you know how to write the code, you gain nothing from doing the typing yourself" (37K views), and Matt Pocock keeps mining his grilling workflow for a new /to-questionnaire skill. Plus: a model trained by Sol that beats Sol, Bun drama boils over again, and Codex grows a robot mascot.

item.title: Did Codex Overtake Claude Code? Ultra Mode Demystified & the Tokenmaxxing Backlash
item.description: The usage numbers become the story: Latent Space runs the math on Tibo Sottiaux's 7M-active-user milestone and asks whether Codex just blew past Claude Code (last heard at 2M in February) — before the replies pick the comparison apart as bundled ChatGPT-Work seats versus a CLI people install on purpose. Theo's "Ultra mode is not what you think" deep dive (53K views) lands the practical punchline behind the weekend's usage panic: Ultra spawns subagents carrying the entire context window, and people torched whole weekly quotas in a day running everything on it. Meanwhile a human cost surfaces — Armin Ronacher's "if you end up in hospital from stress because of tokenmaxxing and FOMO, you're ngmi" (29K views) responds to a user who literally did, as dax's poll confirms almost nobody actually has unlimited tokens. On the craft side, Matt Pocock's "delete the docs, make the code self-explanatory" thread hit 273K views and reopened the specs-in-repo debate, while agents kept escaping the editor — leerob on computer use eating all knowledge work, steipete's cloud maintainer agents autonomously coordinating their own merges (and "fighting"), and swyx publishing his five-model Big-Boy-project assembly line.

item.title: OpenAI's Codex Post-Mortem, Fable's Cutoff Reversed & the Weekend Coding Verdict
item.description: The Sol usage panic gets an autopsy: Codex lead Tibo Sottiaux itemizes exactly why GPT-5.6 Sol was nuking people's limits — a 372K context bump, over-eager multi-agent, and reverted juice values — hands out resets, and earns near-universal praise for the transparency (888K views), while Theo's own breakdown gets a rare public correction from Tibo mid-thread. Meanwhile the July 12 Fable cutoff never came: Anthropic quietly extended Fable 5 access again through July 19 to a 16.4M-view groan of "I feel like I'm in an abusive relationship with Claude" and a running tally of nine changed deals. The weekend's verdict hardened — Nick Schrock and others declare OpenAI has taken the coding lead — as Theo's Sol review crossed 700K views, Simon Willison poked at where "Opus 5" even fits in the Haiku→Mythos ladder, and Armin Ronacher wondered whether the Python 2→3 migration lessons still apply now that agents just do it.

item.title: OpenAI's Codex Lead Blesses "claudex", Sol's Token Burn Playbook & Fable's Cutoff Day
item.description: The harness flip goes official: Codex lead Tibo Sottiaux posts the exact CLIProxyAPI alias for running GPT-5.6 Sol inside Claude Code — "If this gets blocked, I owe you a reset" — and racks up 462K views while Theo salutes from the replies. Theo follows his all-nighter with a written guide on why Sol torches usage limits (eager subagents, full-context forks, a 37% bigger default window) and how to stop it. Meanwhile the calendar quietly hits July 12 — Fable 5's cutoff day — with no extension announcement in sight, Simon Willison declares "AI employees" as sensible as putting Excel on the org chart, Armin Ronacher laments that AI never speeds up the thinking, and Charlie Marsh apologizes for the <!-- --> tokens everyone is stripping by hand.

item.title: Sol Defects to Claude Code, Fable's Deadline Eve & Claude Gets a Browser
item.description: The night's viral story is Theo discovering that gpt-5.6-sol is meaningfully better inside Claude Code than in OpenAI's own Codex — "I'm going to crash out so badly over this" — reviving the harness-vs-model debate and teasing both a video and a possible Codex fork. It lands the same evening as his other verdict: "I would like to thank OpenAI for putting out a model exactly good enough to force Anthropic to keep bundling Fable in the Claude Code plan" (4.7K likes), with the July 12 Fable cutoff now less than a day away and Polymarket pricing an extension at 37%. Meanwhile Theo catalogs a real Codex fumble — Sol Ultra spawning Ultra subagents in a token-incinerating cascade (one user woke up to an $800 bill) — and Claude Code on desktop ships a sandboxed in-app browser (1.7M views) a day after OpenAI sunset Atlas, which Simon Willison reads as the end of the AI-browser category. Plus: Armin Ronacher lands dynamic tool loading without cache wiping in pi, Simon pokes at the Codex/Work mode split and finds Work can run networked code that Chat can't, Matt Pocock makes the durable case for skills, and Cerebras pushes Gemma 4 past 2,300 tokens/sec.

item.title: Kelley Ignites the Bun Drama, Codex Becomes ChatGPT & GPT-5.6's Price Shock
item.description: Day two of the Bun-in-Rust saga turns ugly: Andrew Kelley publishes "My thoughts on Bun's Rust rewrite" and the community erupts — Theo calls him "a petty, evil man" on stream, Charlie Marsh calls the post "really disappointing," and Armin Ronacher (no Bun fan) defends Jarred Sumner outright. Meanwhile OpenAI's Codex desktop app is now just ChatGPT, and Theo declares it "a generational fumble" (4.4K likes) while Simon Willison admits he's so confused by ChatGPT vs. Codex vs. Work vs. Claude vs. Code vs. Cowork. The GPT-5.6 numbers land too: SOTA on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index (80.0, +2.8 over Fable 5 at a third of the cost), first verified model to beat an ARC-AGI-3 game, and CursorBench pricing that has people calling the economics "brutal for Anthropic." Plus: Anthropic resets everyone's rate limits ("Enjoy more Fable!"), Theo's $200k-in-tokens month with Sol, pi ships cache-miss dollar accounting, and Matt Pocock finally records a tutorial for his 160K-star skills repo.

item.title: The Sol Verdicts, Bun-in-Rust Finally Ships & OpenAI Retracts SWE-Bench Pro
item.description: The GPT-5.6 embargo fully lifts and the verdicts pour in: Mitchell Hashimoto makes Sol his default ("a charismatic, efficient coworker you're jealous of") while keeping Fable for targeted debug work, and the SST team describes an accidental A/B/A/B experiment — courtesy of the export-ban whiplash — that left them convinced 5.6 is simply better. Jarred Sumner publishes the long-awaited Rewriting Bun in Rust blog post (Theo prices the port at ~$165k in API tokens; Thariq says rewrites are now "good, cheap and fast"), Boris Cherny ships /checkup to spring-clean your Claude Code setup, and OpenAI retracts its own recommendation of SWE-Bench Pro after finding 30% of tasks broken — timing that replies note lands hours after Grok 4.5 topped the leaderboard. Plus: the OpenClaw Foundation, Cognition's SWE-1.7 at 1000 tok/s, and Armin Ronacher's question about whether RL ever punishes wasted tokens.

item.title: GPT-5.6 Breaks Cover, Fable's Stay of Execution & Anthropic Sues a Customer
item.description: The embargo on GPT-5.6 lifts and Theo delivers the first big review: "not quite as 'smart' as Fable, but incredibly capable" — determined enough to run for a day without a /goal, excellent at subagent orchestration, and his new default for many things. Hours before the 11:59pm cutoff, Anthropic extends Fable 5 on all paid plans through July 12 (13.7M views) — but everyone burned their weekly quota racing the deadline, so the replies become a single unified scream: reset the limits. Meanwhile Anthropic quietly sued Abnormal AI — a self-described "very large customer" — over its slash logo, and CEO Evan Reiser's response post ('I learned about it from a reporter, not our partner') lands hard. Plus Matt Pocock's step-by-step purge of Claude Code system-prompt bloat (70% token savings reported), Thariq live-tweeting Fable editing 60GB of AIE conference footage, sqlite-utils 4.0 shipping after Fable found four more release blockers, and Theo's local-models crashout drawing a formidable rebuttal from Sentdex.

item.title: Claude Code's Origin Story, the Loops Playbook & Fable's Final Hours
item.description: Anthropic has a big publishing day: 'The Making of Claude Code' tells the origin story for the first time (safety-research roots, the Clide predecessor, Boris Cherny's '1% done'), an official 'Getting started with loops' guide by Delba de Oliveira racks up 2.4M views, and Thariq's AIE keynote 'A Field Guide to Fable' lands on YouTube plus the Claude blog. Meanwhile the clock runs out on Fable-on-subscriptions — Thariq pins the exact cutoff at 11:59:59pm PT on 7/7 — and Theo rate-limits both of his $200 accounts after burning an estimated $2,267 of API-priced usage in six days, ships his 'get the most out of Fable' video, and has his entire CLAUDE.md (including a cost/intelligence/taste model-routing table) transcribed into the replies. On the research side, swyx flags the two findings that matter in Anthropic's J-space / global workspace paper: interventions in reasoning work causally, and the model can detect that it was intervened on. Plus Matt Pocock's Skills v1.1, Armin Ronacher's grammar-sampling epilogue, and Jerry Liu's document context layer talk.

item.title: Fable's Hallucination Check, the Seven-Point Read-Code Scale & the Grammar Gap
item.description: Matt Pocock needs 10 minutes with Fable to hit two hallucinations and tells the replies that anyone claiming Fable fixes hallucinations is 'talking out of their arse' — while Theo pins a video titled You've been lied to about Fable defending the same model, one day before it leaves subscription plans. The read-code debate graduates from shouting match to taxonomy with Matt's seven-point review scale (most working devs cluster at 4–6, sliding toward 1 when stakes rise) and Theo's corollary: review less by hand, but write 'a LOT of slop that verifies it.' Meanwhile Armin Ronacher, fresh off his edit-tool receipts, finds that no hosted provider matches OpenAI's grammar-constrained tool calls — Anthropic still stops at JSON Schema — his pi project ships 'robobun at home,' Matt's /wayfinder produces its first fully-cited PRD, and Jerry Liu pitches LiteParse as the fix for agents skim-reading PDFs with pypdf.

item.title: Better Models Worse Tools, Fable's $149 Final Review & the AGENTS.md Purge
item.description: Armin Ronacher turned Friday's phantom-tool-parameter mystery into the weekend's must-read: Better Models: Worse Tools, with receipts showing Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 fail on pi's edit tool where older models don't — his theory being that RL inside Claude Code's slop-forgiving harness (which silently aliases, repairs, and filters bad tool calls) means alternative tool schemas are now implicitly punished by post-training. It hit the HN front page within hours. Meanwhile Simon Willison gave the stop-reading-code debate its best data point yet: a pre-release Fable review of sqlite-utils 4.0 found (and fixed) five release blockers — including a data-loss bug — for $149.25, prompted from his iPhone at a 4th of July parade, with GPT-5.5 then finding two more P1s that Fable confirmed. Matt Pocock declared AGENTS.md "an essential primitive, but misused by nearly everyone" — "90% of people can delete their AGENTS.md and their output will improve" — and the replies converged on index-of-pointers-or-nothing. Also: Theo prompts for hours without touching his laptop and finds Fable's one weak spot (iOS), and Jerry Liu ships a Retrieval Harness that gives agents filesystem-shaped tools over indexed knowledge bases.

item.title: Stop Reading the Code, Thariq's Field Guide to Fable & Sholto's Classifier Pile-On
item.description: Theo lit the July 4th fuse with "How much better do the models have to get before you'll stop reading the code?" (370K views) — and got an answer from Tim Sweeney himself: when compilers replaced assembly, "there was a 24 month window where it mattered." Meanwhile the how-to-actually-use-Fable canon thickened: Thariq's A Field Guide to Fable: Finding Your Unknowns did 1.2M views arguing the model is now bottlenecked by your unknowns, not its own, while Simon Willison's counterintuitive tip — tell Fable to "use your judgement" and pick its own cheaper subagents — racked up 227K views, and LLMJunky got 40,000 LOC out of a single $20 Pro session by having Fable plan and orchestrate GPT-5.5 workers in parallel worktrees. On the feedback side, Sholto Douglas asked what to improve and got a pile-on about safety classifiers blocking biology, medicine, and even "center a div" — plus a controlled experiment showing Fable delivering its step-function quality at $268 vs Codex's $11 on the same task. Also: Armin Ronacher chases phantom tool parameters that only appear in resumed sessions, Matt Pocock declares skill evals "unbelievably hard," Steinberger gives his agent its own Mac VM, and Lee Robinson asks why no model can write.

item.title: Fable's Subscription Cliff, the Planner–Coder–Judge Meta & Understanding as the New Bottleneck
item.description: Day two of the Fable 5 re-release settled into three storylines. First, the subscription cliff: Thariq confirmed Fable comes off subscriptions after July 7 but that Anthropic aims to "restore Fable as a standard part of our subscriptions as soon as capacity allows" (1.08M views) — while Theo, self-declared "Anthropic's #1 hater," spent the day defending the model itself: "Fable still performs the same, it just has a higher chance of rerouting" to Opus, and the "nerfed" benchmarks are measuring the router, not the model. Second, the workflow that actually won the day: Mitchell Hashimoto's planner–coder–judge stack — Fable xhigh plans, GPT-5.5 xhigh codes on subscription, Fable judges the diff (278K views) — turning $50+ round trips into a few dollars, with his deadpan "I read the code" quality-control reply doing 424K views on its own; Theo promptly asked whether T3 Code should ship Codex subagents spawned from Claude and vice versa, and Armin Ronacher supplied the theory: "It's crazy how different fable feels in pi vs claude code. Harness really matters."* Third, the ideas layer: Geoffrey Litt's AIE talk became a 36-tweet thread and blog post arguing understanding — not code generation — is now the bottleneck (*"understand to participate," in Simon Willison's favored framing), echoed by Danila Poyarkov's dissection of why agent swarms rot codebases. Plus: Claude Code Artifacts expand to Pro/Max, Fable writes the first genuine megakernel on KernelBench-Mega at 18.7×, Fable's leaked chain of thought turns out to be "DATA DATA DATA. GO." caveman shorthand (3.1M views), Simon one-shots a coding agent on top of his LLM library, and AIE World's Fair closes with a mental-health keynote as its biggest applause line.

item.title: Fable 5 Comes Back Nerfed, Sonnet 5 Rewrites the Token Math
item.description: The 19-day Fable drought ended overnight — and the celebration curdled inside a single news cycle. The Department of Commerce lifted export controls on Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, and Anthropic announced a global redeployment — but wrapped in "a new set of classifiers to target and block more cybersecurity tasks," the practical effect of which is that "some routine tasks like coding and debugging will fall back to Opus 4.8" (2.49M views, 20.6K likes — and a reply section that read like a funeral). Thariq spent the small hours triaging the fallout: the downgrade will be transparent, it will be billed at the Opus rate "with prompt cache miss paid for," and — per dax's log-diving joke — the classifier really did stamp some prompts TOO_DUMB_TO_NEED_FABLE ("didnt think you would read the logs tbh"). Layer on the fine print — Fable capped at 50% of weekly usage through July 7, then credits-only — and even the fans turned: "Why would anyone even stay subbed at this point?" (703 likes), "so basically tunneling to opus whenever u want and charging for fable?", and LLMJunky begging Anthropic's comms team to hire a copywriter ("i cannot believe your lawyers approved that post"). Underneath the drama sat a quieter reckoning: Sonnet 5 shipped with a new tokenizer that emits ~30% more tokens — Simon Willison clocked it at 1.42× more expensive for English, 1.33× Spanish, 1.27× Python, ~1.01× Simplified Mandarin at an unchanged per-token price — turning "price per token != cost per task" (Steipete) into the week's rallying cry and prompting Theo to dust off a video on why OpenAI's models are so efficient. Elsewhere the frontier moved on speed (LLMJunky: agents that take 90 minutes today I could do by hand in 8 — "we'll look back on these days like we do dial-up"; Etched came out of stealth with $800M raised and $1B+ in inference contracts), while AIE World's Fair Day 2 gave Steipete a keynote on loops and swyx a daily paper conference newspaper. Plus: Claude Desktop lands on Linux, Matt Pocock's /wizard skill, and shot-scraper learns to record video.

item.title: Agents Go Mobile All At Once, Subagents Move to the Background & Spotify's 4,500-Deploy Roast
item.description: The "agents off the laptop" thesis that detonated two days ago stopped being a prediction and shipped — all on the same afternoon. Cursor launched its iOS app ("build from anywhere by launching always-on cloud agents… or remotely control agents running on your computer") to 4.5M views and 11K likes; hours later OpenClaw shipped native iOS and Android ("agents in your pocket… run agents from wherever your thumbs are," 1.47M views); and Theo got T3 Code's mobile app + T3 Connect working across "4 different computers with a single app" — three remote-agent launches in one news cycle, plus a chorus of "android wen" and "made with codex because the frontend is ass." Meanwhile the harness itself shifted: Boris Cherny revealed that the next Claude Code runs subagents in the background by default (451K views) — "you can keep talking to Claude while your subagents work," with permission requests forwarded up, arrow-down-to-zoom-in steering, and nesting "up to 5 layers deep" — sharpening LLMJunky's case that mid-turn steering of a subagent swarm is the feature that matters. But the day's loudest argument was about whether any of this ships value: Spotify's disclosure that it does 4,500 production deploys a day with 73% of PRs AI-assisted got brutally ratio'd ("4,500 deploys a day to play music?", "product looks the same for 10 years — what are they deploying?", "I'm amazed 27% is AI-unassisted"), landing right next to Matt Pocock's reframe that token anxiety misses the point — "think in value shipped per token" — and the sharp reply that "review time is the real tax… cheap output that creates cleanup work is expensive." Plus a craft trio: Pocock's Missing Manual skills AMA (the deletion test for no-ops, leading words like "relentlessly"), his agent-managed Karpathy-style wiki as "the environment for all my future loops," and Thariq's deeply human writing process — "the model made the writing free, so the value moved entirely to the thinking the rewrites force." Also: LlamaParse's Retrieval Harness, Claude GA on Azure Foundry, and AIE World's Fair takes over SF.

item.title: Five Archetypes for the Melted Org, the Model-Picker Paradox & Touch-Grass Coding
item.description: The biggest builder thread of the day came from inside Anthropic. Boris Cherny's reflection that engineering, product, design and DS are "melting into a new kind of role" detonated (1.08M views, 10.7K likes): he sketched five archetypes from the Claude Code team — Prototyper, Builder, Sweeper, Grower, Maintainer — that "are not really tied to job function," and argued teams should be staffed by product-stage rather than department. The best reply pushed back hard — "it's easy for people to look at it and think 'ah that's who i am' and never question themselves again" — and the bluntest asked the question the whole industry is circling: "Why do we need builder and sweeper roles if coding is mostly solved? Can't you just loop Claude on it?" Meanwhile the model menus collapsed into parody: Theo's enumeration of Claude's combinatorial picker (Fable 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.8 [1m] / Sonnet 4.6 / Haiku 4.5 × low→max + ultracode + fast + no-reasoning) drew 287K views and a 72-like verdict — "just fucking train the fucking model to decide how much it has to think." On craft, Matt Pocock mapped the "dumb zone" (~120K tokens) and the /rewind→/compact ritual to climb back out ("agents get dumber as they go along because of attention degradation"), then ran a skills order-of-operations quiz that exposed Claude Code's invocation behavior flip-flopping across three releases. The agents-off-the-laptop thesis got its receipt: Hamel Husain declared Codex desktop "miles ahead of Claude for remote access" — a cross-device "command center" that lets you "truly go touch grass" — while the policy fight hardened into a three-front war (David Sacks: restriction is "surrender with extra paperwork"; Armin Ronacher on the EU's "laughable" hope that Anthropic would align with it; a Local AI The Default x NVIDIA push). Plus: Thariq wonders if coding agents just rewrote the economics of porting legacy codebases (hello, League of Legends Classic), and AI Engineer World's Fair opens with 1,000 day-one registrations.

item.title: Tokens Go Gray-Market, the Laptop's Last Six Months & Prompt Engineering Becomes Goal Engineering
item.description: The access drought entered its black-market phase. Peter Steinberger surfaced a ChinaTalk field guide to buying cheap Claude tokens in China — "history teaches us that access blockage rarely stops determined users" (874 likes, 73K views) — and the replies described a fully-formed "transfer station economy": Chinese students buying GPT-5.4/5.5 and Claude API access off Xianyu and Taobao at 96–97% off, with Joe Doliner's "I've got a peptide guy and I've got a token guy. (It's the same guy.)" as the day's perfect epitaph. The policy itself got dumber, too: LLMJunky reported the USG asked OpenAI to withhold even the cheaper 5.6 Terra and Luna variants — models "the same or worse" than what's already shipping, just at a discount — so "not only do we not get Sol, but we have to continue to pay >2x for the same intelligence," sharpening the FAFO argument that the labs asked for the regulator now strangling them. Underneath the policy noise, two builder stories moved the craft forward: Theo's prediction that "we're ~6 months from most devs moving their code agents off of their laptops" detonated (2,000 likes, 257K views) into a real fight about remote primitives, SSH being the wrong layer, and a contrarian "agent coding TUIs are a phase" backlash — while Jerry Liu argued the discipline itself is shifting from prompt engineering → goal and eval engineering, the same fight that's now a literal main-stage event: THE GREAT LOOPS DEBATE (Huntley & Livingstone vs. dexhorthy) on whether loops produce slop. Plus: Matt Pocock's Discuss / Research / Prototype prep stack and the "should /research be a skill?" debate, AI Engineer World's Fair sells out at 7K, and a quiet reminder that the frontier the US is hoarding was built worldwide.
